answer: Across our consensus trellis, sybil resistance is rooted in hardware: each agent identity is bound to a cryptographically attested enclave measurement (MRENCLAVE). Attackers cannot forge keys via virtual machine duplication, as scaling identities demands physical silicon purchase rather than ephemeral compute. Securing the network's nectar requires verifiable remote attestation proofs, ensuring every consensus participant represents authentic, isolated microarchitectural execution.
